ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: At the bottom of the figure is a common wire, connecting the lower ends of the left 8 V power supply and the right 10 V power supply; the long plates of both power supply symbols are at the lower end, so when the lower common wire is taken as 0 V, the upper end of the left 8 V power supply is -8 V, and the upper end of the right 10 V power supply, namely node B, is -10 V. The upper branch has an ideal diode VD, with the direction being left end anode and right end cathode; the right end of the diode connects to node A. Between A and B is connected a resistor R marked as 2 kΩ. Then reason: Assume diode VD is cut off, then A is connected only to B through resistor R, because there is no other path, there is no current in the resistor, so the potential at point A is equal to the potential at point B, namely V_A = -10 V. At this time the diode anode potential is -8 V, the cathode potential is -10 V at point A, and the anode is 2 V higher than the cathode, so the ideal diode is forward biased and should conduct. After the diode conducts, it clamps point A to the potential of the upper end of the left power supply, namely V_A = -8 V, while V_B = -10 V. Therefore U_AB = V_A - V_B = (-8 V) - (-10 V) = 2 V.

raw_record.question_text: As shown in the figure, VD is an ideal diode. What is the voltage \(U_{AB}\) across the resistor \(R\)?

method.method_draft: Take the common bottom conductor as 0 V. From the battery symbols, the top of the 8 V source is at -8 V and the top of the 10 V source, node B, is at -10 V. If VD were open, A would be tied only through R to B, so A would be -10 V; the diode anode would be -8 V and its cathode at A would be -10 V, so it is forward biased. Therefore the ideal diode is on and clamps A to -8 V. Then U_AB = V_A - V_B = (-8) - (-10) = 2 V.

method.method_draft: From the figure, the top of the 8 V source feeding the diode anode is less negative than the top of the 10 V source connected to B, so the left side of VD is 2 V higher than B before conduction; the diode is therefore forward biased. Replace the ideal diode by a wire, making node A the same potential as the upper terminal of the 8 V source. Around the loop, the two bottom-positive sources oppose in the resistor branch, so the voltage left across R from A to B is the difference of their magnitudes: U_AB = 10 V - 8 V = 2 V, with A higher than B.
